title: Split-traffic rollback & KV-cache reconciliation plan for hybrid model regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a concise, operational runbook to perform split-traffic rollbacks when a model rollout causes regressions that manifest differently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Key complexity: tenants may have per-tenant KV/prefix caches and asymmetric model variants (quantized vs full-precision). A naive rollback risks cache/sequence mismatches and customer-visible inconsistencies. This ticket defines the orchestration and KV-cache reconciliation steps, the communication path for affected customers, and testable rollback commands for engineers and SREs.

Background and motivation:
- Multiple recent incidents surfaced a pattern: canary traffic triggered a regression that only impacted longer-context requests and caused subtle tokenization/formatting regressions.
- Dedicated and Private tenants sometimes run a different model artifact (quantized build) which made a straight rollback produce divergent outputs due to cached KV states and different decode paths.
- Customers saw partial failures: some requests succeeded, others had degraded outputs, leading to escalations.

Impact:
- Customer-facing regressions across a small subset of tenants.
- Potential data residency concerns for Private deployments if stateful workarounds are applied inconsistently.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Provide an operator-safe, repeatable split-traffic rollback procedure that minimizes customer disruption.
2) Define KV/prefix cache reconciliation and cache invalidation heuristics tied to rollback.
3) Create communication templates for SRE/CS to use during escalations.
4) Produce a small automation script (rollback-helper) to run the most common steps with audit logging.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runbook validated in a staging mirror of Dedicated + Hosted + a simulated Private environment.
- Automation script present with unit tests and a dry-run mode.
- Communication templates reviewed by Support and Legal.

Runbook (operator steps):
1) Triage & scope: identify impacted model variant, affected deployment types, and tenant slice. Use dashboards: Console -> Rollouts -> Model X -> Canary metrics and trace links.
2) Quarantine canary: if still progressing, pause or reduce canary slice to 0% for outgoing traffic using the rollouts API. Command: curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/{rollout_id}/pause -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\"
3) Snapshot state: capture current model artifact hashes and KV cache metrics per node. Commands: 
   - curl https://infra.internal/api/nodes?env=dedicated -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -> save to /tmp/rollback-snapshot.json
   - redis-cli --rdb /tmp/redis-snapshot.rdb (for tenants using shared Redis)
4) Determine rollback target: prefer previous stable artifact that matches quantization profile of the current tenant pool. If hosted had a different artifact than dedicated, choose per-environment target. Record chosen artifact id in the rollback audit log.
5) Prepare cache strategy (choose one):
   - Soft-restart (preferred when KV incompatibility is unlikely): perform model swap, then allow KV warmup. Monitor a validation pingset for 30 minutes.
   - Targeted cache flush (when architecture mismatch): issue per-tenant prefix invalidation and restart the worker(s) serving that tenant slice. Commands: POST /internal/cache/invalidate with tenant_id and prefix list.
   - Cold-start (last resort for stubborn divergence): full worker restart with cache wipe. This will increase latency temporarily; pre-notify customers.
6) Execute model swap on small tenant slice first (staged rollback): route 10% of affected tenants to the rollback artifact and run validation pings. If green, increment to 50%, then 100%.
7) KV-cache reconciliation details:
   - Checkpoints: before targeted invalidation, export recent KV keys for affected prefix window (last 48h). If keys are critical (session continuation), store them in a reconciliation staging store.
   - Reapply strategy: after rollback, rehydrate only keys that match pre-rollback decode expectations. For safety, rehydrate deterministic stateless entries (e.g., feature-rollout flags).
   - Avoid reapplying ephemeral generation-state keys (e.g., per-request attention cache handles) to prevent mismatched hidden-state.
8) Verification: run the customer-facing prompt set (shared in runbook artifacts) against both the pre-rollback and post-rollback endpoints and compare token-level diffs. Use the eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness PR #245.
9) Customer communication: publish a short triage note to #customer-incidents and send templated messages to CS contacts. Use templates in Confluence -> \"Rollback customer templates\".
10) Post-rollback monitoring: keep increased sampling (trace and output diffs) for 72 hours and open a follow-up ticket for root-cause remediation.

Automation: rollback-helper (requirements):
- Dry-run mode that prints intended commands.
- Integrations: Rollouts API, Cache API, infra node snapshot API, and Slack webhook for audit messages.
- Must write an audit entry to /var/log/redwood/rollback-audit.log with timestamp, operator, tenant slice, artifacts involved, and chosen cache strategy.

Testing plan:
- Stage mirror run: simulate traffic split using the canary rig and validate the KV reconciliation choices against a seeded Redis instance.
- Chaos run: automate a test where the host artifact differs from the dedicated artifact and ensure the runbook calls the targeted cache flush path.

Communication templates (examples in Confluence):
- Initial message to affected customers: short explanation, mitigation plan, expected timeframe, contact.
- Post-mitigation summary: what happened, what was rolled back, and any required customer actions.

Escalation & handoff notes:
- If regression persists after staged rollback, escalate to oncall SRE + inference core (+1 from runtime) and open incident bridge with a priority annotation.
- For Private deployments, coordinate with customer infra admin to run cache invalidation if we cannot reach their Redis/HSM. Document a signed approval if we request remote access.

Incident log (updates):
- 2026-02-15 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after triage on incident INC-2026-0215. Initial draft of runbook and KV strategies.
- 2026-02-16 Marcelo Rivera: Added targeted cache flush commands and the snapshot play. Requested review from Support (Emma Liu) and Legal (Ravi Menon).
- 2026-02-17 Emma Liu (Support): Reviewed communication templates; suggested minor wording changes to the initial customer message to reduce technical terms.
- 2026-02-18 SRE review (Jamal Ortiz): Recommended adding a dry-run for rollback-helper and an explicit 5-minute cool-down between staged increments.
- 2026-02-20 Marcelo Rivera: Added the rollback-helper requirements and updated acceptance criteria.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- ENG: implement rollback-helper + unit tests (owner: Marcelo) (ETA: 2 weeks).
- SRE: add canary validation pingset to Console (owner: Jamal) (ETA: 1 week).
- Support: finalize customer templates and SLA messaging (owner: Emma) (ETA: 3 business days).
- Security: verify Private deployment access policy for cache operations (owner: Ravi) (ETA: 1 week).

Links / artifacts: list of operational artifacts and PRs:
- Runbook in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Split-Traffic-Rollback-Runbook
- Rollback-helper prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tools/pull/412 (draft)
- Eval harness pingset: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/main/pingsets/rollback-validation
- Incident INC-2026-0215 timeline: https://incident.redwood.ai/INC-2026-0215
- Slack channel for coordination: #inc-2026-0215

Notes on uniqueness / trade-offs considered: 
- We intentionally prefer targeted cache invalidation over full wipes when possible to limit downstream cold-start latency. However, targeted invalidation increases complexity and requires safe rehydration heuristics.
- For Private deployments, manual customer coordination introduces slower mitigation but preserves customer autonomy and data residency guarantees.

Owner notes: Marcelo will carve out the rollback-helper MVP and demo it in the next SRE sync. After validation in the staging mirror, we'll run a tabletop exercise with Support and SRE to validate the communication workflow.

Audit trail requirement: every live rollback must append a single-line JSON entry to /var/log/redwood/rollback-audit.log with fields: timestamp, operator, key, tenant_slice, rollback_artifact, cache_strategy, dry_run=false.
